strings.title: Messages from the Raven
strings.hint: The Raven is dead... so who sent the next blackmail message? Track whoever rented the new server that received the archive on the night of the crime.
strings.solvedText:
Culprit: technical assistant Zaid Qarman.

The Raven was not killed by one of his victims, but by his apprentice. Zaid maintained the blackmail infrastructure for scraps. He saw the archive as a gold mine that deserved a cleverer operator. On the night of the crime, he copied the entire archive to a server rented under a stolen identity, killed his mentor, and took the encrypted device. Then greed made him careless: two days after the death, he sent a new blackmail message imitating the Raven's style — to a victim whose file the Raven had secretly closed a month earlier.

What convicted him: the overnight transfer log, a telltale habit in the imitation message's wording, and a storage-server payment from a wallet traced back to him.
strings.summary.text: Imad N., known in the shadows as 'the Raven,' blackmailed half the city's wealthy with an archive of scandals. He was found murdered in his fortified apartment, his encrypted device missing and his safe opened with the correct code, without tampering. The potential suspects? Almost every one of his victims. But two days after his death, one victim received another blackmail message... in the Raven's own style.

strings.summary.victim.name: Imad N. — 'the Raven'
strings.summary.victim.note: A victim with no sympathizers — and a city-long list of enemies
strings.summary.timeline[0].l: Last call to his technical assistant
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: Archive copied to an external server
strings.summary.timeline[3].l: A new blackmail message in his style
strings.scene.address: Fortified apartment — top floor of a residential tower
strings.scene.intro: An armored door without forced entry and a safe opened with its code: the culprit belonged to a very small inner circle. The main encrypted device is missing. Network records show a massive transfer minutes before the death. The Raven never copied his own archive; he considered it a 'security sin.'
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Recording and encryption equipment in his office
strings.scene.notes[0]: Safe opened with the correct code — no tampering
strings.scene.notes[1]: Complete archive copied at 23:15 to an unknown server
strings.scene.notes[2]: The main encrypted device is missing
strings.scene.notes[3]: A new blackmail message sent two days after the death
strings.evidence[0].title: Overnight Transfer Log
strings.evidence[0].desc: 1.8 terabytes transferred to a server rented 3 days earlier under a stolen identity.
strings.evidence[1].title: The Imitation Message
strings.evidence[1].desc: A convincing imitation of the Raven's style... but it targets a victim whose file he secretly closed a month earlier — information known only inside the operation.
strings.evidence[2].title: The Open Safe
strings.evidence[2].desc: Opened with the correct code. The Raven changed it a week earlier and gave it to just one person 'for emergencies.'
strings.evidence[3].title: Digital Payment Wallet
strings.evidence[3].desc: Paid the server rental. Earlier transactions connect it to the assistant's salary wallet.
strings.evidence[4].title: The Businessman's Threats
strings.evidence[4].desc: The Raven's biggest victim sent this a week earlier: 'Your final price, or your funeral.' A conspicuous lead.
strings.evidence[5].title: The Journalist's Notes
strings.evidence[5].desc: A journalist threatened by the archive was preparing an investigation exposing the Raven's identity.
strings.suspects[0].name: Businessman Ghanem Zahr
strings.suspects[0].relation: The biggest blackmail victim — paid millions
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'At my farm with my family — twenty witnesses and cameras.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: Did I threaten him? Yes. Who would not threaten his tormentor? But I buy my solutions; I do not kill them. His death is the worst thing that could happen to me. My file is now held by a ghost whose price I do not even know.
strings.suspects[1].name: Zaid Qarman
strings.suspects[1].relation: The Raven's technical right hand for 4 years
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I was patching our servers from home — my work logs prove it.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: Imad taught me everything and was as harsh as a miserly father. I was the last person to speak to him alive. He asked me to investigate a possible leak, and I went to sleep afterward. The overnight transfer? Perhaps he did it himself when he suspected someone was closing in.
strings.suspects[2].name: Journalist Mayar Asaad
strings.suspects[2].relation: Threatened by the archive while pursuing his identity
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'At the newspaper office finishing my investigation, with editors beside me until dawn.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: I was a week away from publishing his real name and photograph. His murder destroyed the scoop of my life and turned my investigation into an obituary. Whoever killed him wanted the archive alive and the Raven dead — the exact opposite of what I needed.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Tower security guard
strings.witnesses[0].statement: No stranger went up that night. Apart from the resident, only his young assistant had elevator access to the top floor. He went up and came down shortly before midnight.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Top-floor neighbor
strings.witnesses[1].statement: I heard a muffled argument, then silence. Afterward came the sound of a small suitcase rolling across the tiles toward the elevator.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Victim 'S.'
strings.witnesses[2].statement: I paid the Raven for years. Then, a month ago, he surprised me with a strange message: 'Your file is closed — consider it retirement.' Whoever contacted me after his death does not know that... so it is not him.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Body discovery report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: The weekly cleaner reported the death. The door was locked without forced entry, and the apartment was tidy except for the office.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Crime Scene Report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: A fatal blow from behind with a blunt object while he sat at his computer. The killer stood behind him with the confidence of someone who did so every day.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Message Style Analysis
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: A superficial imitation: the same template, but with programming-style punctuation — semicolons — that the Raven never used.
strings.folders[2].name: Interviews
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Businessman Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: Farm cameras confirm his absence. He offered a reward for recovering the archive: anxiety, not remorse.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Assistant Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: His 'home work logs' were manually fabricated after midnight. He denied knowing the new safe code, then was identified as the 'emergency contact' in the Raven's note.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Journalist Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body: Her presence at the newspaper on the night of the crime is documented. She cooperated by handing over her complete draft investigation.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Tracing the Rented Server
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: The server was rented under a stolen identity, but paid for with a digital wallet funded twice from Zaid's salary wallet.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Top-Floor Elevator Log
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: Zaid's access pass: up at 23:02, down at 23:56 carrying a small equipment bag, as recorded by the lobby camera.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: The Raven's Final Note
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: The final line in a paper notebook: 'The boy has grown greedy. I changed the code and gave it to him as bait. If the safe is opened, it is him.' The Raven set the trap... and died before he could testify.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Server Seizure Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: The complete archive was seized before any further blackmail could be put into operation and delivered under seal to the prosecution.
strings.reports[0].title: Inner Circle Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: The safe code, elevator authorization, and knowledge of closed files: three circles with only one person at their intersection.
strings.reports[1].title: The Message That Set the Trap
strings.reports[1].author: Digital Crime Unit
strings.reports[1].body: The posthumous message was the culprit's fatal mistake. It proved the archive still existed and that its holder did not know the Raven's latest arrangements.
strings.notes[0].text: Who knows the new safe code? One person
strings.notes[1].text: The Raven never uses semicolons — a programmer's fingerprint
